name: Scorzonera
grown_as: Scorzonera (black salsify), a perennial usually grown as a biennial for its long black-skinned white-fleshed root. Roots can be lifted in the first autumn or left a second year to thicken, when the plant flowers.
habit: Year 1: a rosette of long, lance-shaped leaves 30 to 50 cm. Year 2: a branched, leafy flowering stem 60 to 100 cm, each branch ending in one flower head. Milky sap.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the root top; alternate up the stem, smaller and narrower above
leaf.outline: Long lance-shaped, 20 to 40 cm by 2 to 5 cm, widest about the middle or above, broader than salsify
leaf.base: Narrowing gradually into a winged stalk that clasps the stem
leaf.veins: A pale midrib with several faint near-parallel veins running along the leaf
leaf.surface: Smooth or with a few soft hairs when young, not waxy
leaf.stalk: Short, winged, merging into the blade
leaf.colour: Mid to dark green, not grey

flower.form: A dandelion-like head made only of strap-shaped florets
flower.petals: Many strap-shaped florets, each ending in five tiny teeth, the outer ones longest
flower.centre: Inner florets shorter, the same yellow
flower.behind: Several rows of overlapping green bracts, pointed, much SHORTER than the florets, forming a narrow cup
flower.carried: One head at the tip of each branch, facing up, on a long stalk
flower.season: May to July of the second year

fruit: A round clock of pale, slim, ribbed seeds, each with a dirty-white feathery parachute, smaller than salsify's.
seedling: Two long, narrow seed leaves, then lance-shaped true leaves broader than salsify's.
winter: Leaves die back in hard frost to a small crown; roots are hardy and left in the ground to lift when needed.

leaf: a long lance-shaped leaf, broader than grass, pointed
base narrowing into a winged clasping stalk
bloom: a head of yellow strap-shaped florets only, no disc
overlapping green bracts shorter than the florets
seed: a long slim ribbed pale seed, about 1.5 cm, with a parachute
young: a rosette of long lance-shaped green leaves
crop: a long straight root with near-black skin, about 2 cm thick and 25 to 40 cm long
white flesh where cut or broken
a rosette of lance-shaped leaves on top
flower: a branched leafy stem with yellow dandelion-like heads, one per branch tip
seedhead: a round clock of feathery parachutes

look_alikes: Salsify has grass-like grey leaves, purple heads with long star-like bracts and a pale root. Dandelion and cat's-ear have toothed or lobed leaves and hollow or leafless flower stalks. Viper's-grass (Scorzonera humilis) is a small wild relative.
